skills.name: Physical quantities, SI units, prefixes and standard form

note.text:
A physical quantity can be measured and has a number and a unit: 25 kg, 3.5 m.
Base quantities and SI units: length (metre, m), mass (kilogram, kg), time (second, s), temperature (kelvin, K), electric current (ampere, A).
Derived quantities come from base ones: area (m²), volume (m³), density (kg/m³), speed (m/s).
Prefixes: mega M = 1 000 000, kilo k = 1000, centi c = 1/100, milli m = 1/1000, micro µ = 1/1 000 000.
Standard form: a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10, e.g. 340 000 m = 3.4 × 10⁵ m; 0.0025 s = 2.5 × 10⁻³ s.

sections.heading: What a physical quantity is
sections.text:
Anything we can measure is a physical quantity: the length of a desk, the mass of a bag of rice, the time of a race.
A measurement always has two parts, a number and a unit: {25} kg. Without the unit, "{25}" means nothing.
Scientists everywhere use the SI system so that results can be shared. Its base quantities are length (m), mass (kg), time (s), temperature (K) and electric current (A). All others, such as area, volume, speed and density, are derived from these.

sections.heading: Prefixes
Standard form
sections.text:
Very large or very small values are written a × {10}ⁿ, with a between {1} and {10}.
• {340000} m = {3.4} × {10}{sup(5)} m (the point moves {5} places left).
• {0.0025} s = {2.5} × {10}⁻{sup(3)} s (the point moves {3} places right, so the power is negative).
The distance from the Earth to the Sun is about {1.5} × {10}{sup(11)} m.

key_words.meaning: something that can be measured, with a number and a unit
a word in front of a unit that multiplies it, like kilo

mistake.why: In standard form the first number must be between {1} and {10}.

worked_example.problem: Write {a * 10 ^ n} m in standard form.
steps: Move the decimal point to get a number between {1} and {10}: {a}.
The point moved {n} places to the left, so the power is {n}.

cards.idea: Every measurement has a number and a unit; the SI unit of mass is the kilogram.
example: Length: metre (m). Time: second (s). Temperature: kelvin (K).

cards.idea: Standard form: a × {10}ⁿ with a between {1} and {10}.

check.prompt: Write {a * 10 ^ n} in standard form, a × {10}ⁿ. What is n?

misconceptions.explain: Count the places the point moves, not the number of digits: {a * 10 ^ n} = {a} × {10}{sup(n)}.

solution: a must be between {1} and {10}: a = {a}.
The decimal point moves {n} places, so n = {answer}.

pick.q: What is the SI unit of mass?
e: The gram is a smaller unit; the SI base unit is the kilogram.
The newton is the unit of force (weight).
pick.y: Mass is measured in kilograms in SI.

pick.q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
e: °C is used every day, but the SI unit is the kelvin.
The joule is the unit of energy.
pick.y: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin.

pick.q: Which is a base quantity (not derived)?
pick.y: Time is one of the base quantities; its unit is the second.

pick.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
pick.y: Current is a base quantity measured in amperes.

misconceptions.explain: Count the places the point moves, not the number of digits: {a * 10 ^ n} = {a} × {10}{sup(n)}.

solution: a must be between {1} and {10}: a = {a}.
The decimal point moves {n} places, so n = {answer}.

misconceptions.explain: A small number (less than {1}) has a negative power of {10}.
{a / 10} is less than {1}: a must be at least {1}.

solution: Move the point right until the number is between {1} and {10}: {a}.
It moved {n} places to the right, so the power is −{n}: {answer}.

questions.prompt: A hair is {d} µm thick. What is this in millimetres?

misconceptions.explain: That is in metres. {1} mm = {1000} µm, so divide by {1000}.
Millimetres are bigger than micrometres: the number gets smaller.
